items.body: Returning a grep error immediately leaves stdin unread. With sufficient pending input, upstream `git grep` receives SIGPIPE; `retired-names.sh:21` prioritizes that status and returns 141 instead of the filter’s error. The previous Python implementation consumed stdin before filtering. A caller reproduction using real `git grep` and an early-exiting filter stub returning 9 produced status 141. Existing tests exercise grep failures directly against xtask, missing this shell interaction.
items.suggestion: Drain the remaining input before returning the filter error, or adjust shell status precedence to preserve filter errors when upstream receives SIGPIPE. Add a shell control with input exceeding pipe capacity and an injected grep failure.
items.title: Returning a grep error immediately leaves stdin unread
